drafts.Draft A:
Brothers and sisters, I want you to know that what has happened to me has actually helped the good news move forward. Everyone in the imperial guard, along with everyone else, now knows that I am in prison because I belong to Christ. My imprisonment has made most of the believers more confident in the Lord, and they now speak God’s message with greater courage and without fear.

Some preach Christ because they are jealous and want to compete with me, while others do it from good motives. Those who act out of love know that I am here to defend the good news. The others preach Christ from selfish ambition and not from sincere motives. They think they can make my imprisonment even harder. But what really matters is that Christ is being proclaimed, whether the motives are false or sincere. That is why I rejoice and will continue to rejoice!
drafts.Draft B:
I want you to know, brothers and sisters, that the things concerning me have turned out rather for the advance of the good news. As a result, it has become clear throughout the whole imperial guard and to everyone else that my imprisonment is in Christ. Most of the brothers and sisters, having become confident in the Lord because of my imprisonment, dare even more to speak the word without fear.

Some proclaim Christ because of envy and rivalry, but others from goodwill. The latter do so from love, knowing that I am appointed for the defense of the good news. The former proclaim Christ from selfish ambition, not sincerely, thinking to stir up trouble for me in my imprisonment. What then? Only this: in every way, whether from false motives or in truth, Christ is proclaimed, and in this I rejoice. Yes, and I will continue to rejoice.
drafts.Draft C:
I want all of you to know, brothers and sisters, that my imprisonment has actually helped the good news move forward. Everyone in the imperial guard, along with the others here, now knows that I am imprisoned because of Christ. Being in prison has made most of the believers here more confident in the Lord. They are more daring to speak God’s message without fear.

Some proclaim Christ out of envy and rivalry, while others do it with good intentions. Those who act out of love know that I am here to defend the good news. But the others proclaim Christ from selfish ambition rather than sincere motives. They think they can add to my suffering while I am in prison. What really matters is that Christ is being proclaimed, whether people speak with false motives or sincere ones. That is why I rejoice and continue to rejoice!
